passage:
Dear Lokesh bhaiya,
I am writing because you are the only one who will not laugh. Since August I have been going to the evening circle at the hostel. They call me family, they remember my birthday, they even wrote me a poem. It felt like coming home. But I have started noticing things. We are told not to tell our parents what is said inside. The leader says part of my stipend should go to "the work", and when I asked where it goes, he said doubt is a lack of faith. I miss how warm the first weeks felt. That is why I am telling you. I am going home this weekend, and I want to talk to Papa. Please call me on Sunday.
Shankar

qa.q: Since when has Shankar been going to the evening circle?
qa.a: Shankar has been going since August.

qa.q: Why does Shankar miss how warm the first weeks felt?
qa.a: Shankar felt real belonging at first, and is torn because that warmth was what drew Shankar in, even though Shankar now sees signs of control.

qa.q: What signs in the group could Shankar check further?
qa.a: Shankar can check whether questions are allowed, whether leaving is free, whether they demand secrecy or money, and keep close ties with family and outside friends.

qa.q: How might Lokesh bhaiya feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Lokesh bhaiya may feel worried but also trusted, since Shankar says he is the only one who will not laugh. The Sunday call gives him a way to stay close.

grounding: A friendly group offers belonging but demands secrecy, money and obedience; the protagonist notices questions are not allowed and keeps family ties.

passage: The monsoon had flooded the lane outside the community hall in Chandigarh, and only eight of them had waded in for Friday circle. Varun, who led the group, smiled at Gurpreet the way he always did, as if nobody else were in the room. For three months the circle had been the warmest place in Gurpreet's week: shared dinners, long talks, people who called each other family. Tonight Varun said the group needed a 'commitment contribution' from each member, and that outsiders, even parents, 'wouldn't understand, so keep it inside.' Gurpreet raised a hand. 'Can I ask what the money is for?' The room went quiet. Varun's smile stayed, but his voice cooled: 'Doubt is how people drift.' Riding home through the rain, Gurpreet phoned his sister and told her everything, then muted the group chat for a week to think with a clear head.

qa.q: How many people waded in for Friday circle?
qa.a: Only eight of them waded in.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel when the room went quiet?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt uneasy and exposed, shaken that a simple question about the money was treated as doubt.
Asking openly about the money, telling his sister everything, and stepping back from the group chat to think.

qa.q: How does Varun seem to see Gurpreet's question?
qa.a: Varun treats it as a threat to the group's hold, cooling his tone and calling it doubt instead of answering it.

grounding: Shows a warm group that asks for money and secrecy, and Gurpreet testing whether questions are allowed and keeping his family close.

passage: Damini had joined the meditation-and-study group in Pune for the free Sunday sessions, and stayed for the feeling of belonging. Sahil, the senior member who first invited her, now texted daily: reminders, praise, 'the family is proud of you.' This weekend was the retreat. It was also Nani's eightieth birthday. 'Real growth means loosening old ties,' Sahil said when she mentioned it, handing her the retreat form. 'Your family keeps you small.' That night Damini sat on a bus-stop bench and ran a test in her head. Could she question the leaders? She had seen how cold they went on the last person who did. Could she skip one retreat without being frozen out? She texted Sahil: 'I'm going to Nani's birthday. I'll miss the retreat.' An hour later: 'Disappointed. Think about where your loyalty is.' Damini called her mother.

qa.q: What did Sahil hand Damini when she mentioned Nani's birthday?
qa.a: Sahil handed her the retreat form.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling on the bus-stop bench?
qa.a: Damini felt uneasy and torn, still drawn to the group's warmth but worried by the pressure to drop her family.

qa.q: What small test helped Damini see the group clearly?
qa.a: Choosing Nani's birthday over one retreat and watching the reaction, which showed that disagreeing or stepping back was not really allowed.

qa.q: How does Sahil see Damini's family?
qa.a: Sahil casts them as a rival loyalty that 'keeps her small', so a birthday visit becomes disloyalty in his eyes.

grounding: Shows a group offering belonging while pushing Damini to drop family ties, and her checking whether she can question or step back and then reaching out to family.
